QF.id: IV Clearing Settlement and Risk Management_26

question.text: How is the Final Settlement Price (FSP) determined for bond futures?

answer.text: Volume Weighted Average Price (VWAP) of the underlying bond on NDS-OM in the last 2 hours of trading, or FIMMDA/FBIL price if NDS-OM data is insufficient
The closing price of the futures contract on the exchange
Simple average of all G-Sec trades on the expiry day
RBI reference rate published on the expiry date

explanation.text: The Logic: Bond futures FSP uses the VWAP from NDS-OM (the OTC G-Sec trading platform) in the last 2 hours. If insufficient trades occur, FIMMDA/FBIL valuation prices are used as fallback. The Trap: The FSP is NOT the futures closing price - it is derived from the underlying cash market. It is not a simple average. RBI does not publish a specific reference rate for this purpose. Cross-Exam Context: FSP methodology varies by product. T-Bill futures use RBI auction yields, MIBOR futures use average daily overnight rates. Know the difference for the exam. Distributor's Pro-Tip: The VWAP methodology ensures the FSP reflects actual market conditions in the underlying bond, preventing manipulation of the futures settlement price.
